subject: DIANNtoMSstatsFormat: proteins quantified only from non-proteotypic (shared) peptides

messages.author: 43483ceb67c5dbff
messages.subject: DIANNtoMSstatsFormat: proteins quantified only from non-proteotypic (shared) peptides
parts:
Dear MSstats community,

I am analyzing DIA-NN 2.7.0 output with MSstats 4.18.1 (R 4.5.0) on a computing cluster. I convert the DIA-NN report with the following call:

input <- DIANNtoMSstatsFormat(input = input,
                              annotation = annot,
                              quantificationColumn = "auto",
                              MBR = TRUE,
                              use_log_file = FALSE)

In the MSstats output, I see proteins that are supported only by shared peptides, i.e. none of their peptides is unique to them. In the DIA-NN report, these peptides are flagged Proteotypic = 0. I had expected that proteins without any proteotypic peptide would not appear in the MSstats output.

Is this expectation correct? Specifically, does DIANNtoMSstatsFormat (with useUniquePeptide = TRUE) use the Proteotypic column of the DIA-NN report to exclude such peptides, or does it only filter on Protein.Group assignment? It seems that DIANN is showing only one ID in "Protein.Group" based on maximum parsimony, but "Protein.Ids" column and "Proteotypic" column clearly shows that identification is based on shared peptide.

Thank you very much for your help.
Best regards,
NIk.

messages.author: 8258b37fa86356b5
messages.subject: Re: DIANNtoMSstatsFormat: proteins quantified only from non-proteotypic (shared) peptides
parts:
Hi Nik,

Your understanding is correct. useUniquePeptide = TRUE does not use the Proteotypic column. Instead, it looks at the protein-peptide pairs after conversion, counts how many different proteins each peptide is assigned to, and keeps only peptides assigned to one protein. So the filter uses the ProteinName column after conversion, not the original DIA-NN report.

The issue is that DIA-NN applies maximum parsimony and reports a single entry in Protein.Group. As a result, a peptide with Proteotypic = 0 can still appear to map to just one protein when the filter is applied. Its count is therefore one, so it passes the filter. This explains why you're seeing proteins supported only by shared peptides.

To get the result you expected, filter the DIA-NN report before conversion:

```

input <- input[input$Proteotypic == 1, ]

```

Then run DIANNtoMSstatsFormat as before.

Thanks for the clear write-up. We will look at whether the converter should read Proteotypic directly.

Best,
Swaraj
